comsupp.lib — Microsoft's COM support library, as linked into lotrbfme.exe
=========================================================================

comsupp.lib
  sha256  b897c136cb2eb0607d4a581f230b0b9cccec9f79c8e736710e359beda42ff45a
  size    294,012 bytes
  from    Visual C++ 7.1 (Visual Studio .NET 2003), Vc7/lib/comsupp.lib

This is a byte-identical copy of the file already committed under
build/toolchains/vs2003/, which is the compiler this repo builds every function
with. It is copied here rather than referenced in place so that ledger rows
name a path without spaces, and so progress.py routes them to the vendored
identity lane the way it does for vendor/d3dx9 — this is Microsoft's compiled
code, not the game's identity.

Why the narrow library and not comsuppw.lib
-------------------------------------------
comsupp.lib and comsuppw.lib compile the same sources for the narrow and wide
wchar_t ABIs and produce byte-identical code, so the bytes cannot choose
between them. Two of the fifteen functions differ in name alone:

    ?ConvertStringToBSTR@_com_util@@YGPAGPBD@Z     (comsupp.lib)
    ?ConvertStringToBSTR@_com_util@@YGPA_WPBD@Z    (comsuppw.lib)

`G` is `unsigned short *` and `_W` is native `wchar_t *`. VC7.1 defaults to
/Zc:wchar_t-, under which wchar_t IS unsigned short and the compiler emits the
`G` spelling; build.py passes no /Zc:wchar_t, so the narrow library is the one
consistent with how everything else here is built.

The debug variants (comsuppd.lib, comsuppwd.lib) were measured too. Only one
body places in unclaimed .text, a 44-byte scalar deleting destructor generic
enough to place by coincidence, and retail is a release build. Not claimed.

Region
------
RVA 0x00AFD550-0x00AFE27A. Fifteen rows cover 3,120 of those 3,370 bytes; each
names the archive member its bytes come from and ./build.sh extracts that
member and byte-compares it against retail like any other row.

Licence
-------
The file is committed as a build input for byte-verification only: it is read
to prove that retail bytes match Microsoft's shipped code, and none of it is
compiled into or redistributed as part of any binary this repo produces.
